request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the tree search, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the main "tree search" test and scenarios 1–3.

**What it does:** there's a search box (`search-name`) and a button (`search`) on the home screen. Pressing the button lists everyone on this sheet and on the other sheets of its tree whose name or an alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. Each match is one line (`search-line`) in the form `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`, and the number of lines shows in `search-count`. The tree means the sheet's parent, that sheet's parent and so on, plus its child sheets and their children; sibling sheets are not searched. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people, sorted by sheet id. Retired people are included. An empty search lists everyone. The old count disappears as soon as the button is pressed again, so two searches with the same result can be told apart.

**Server:** a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` endpoint returns the ids of the other sheets in the tree. It reuses the lookup the name-clash check already does (`NameTree.sheets`), so the two features agree on what the tree is. The files are `tree.GET.yml`, plus `LoadTree`, `Tree` and `RespondWithTree` in the `sheet` package.

**Front end:** the new code is in `features/search/TreeSearch.tsx`, and `features/search/home.slot.tsx` puts it on the home screen. The due-total uses the same calculation as the person row. For the other sheets it reads what the store holds now and uses each sheet's own today and rules, the same way the consolidated figures do.

One behaviour to know: this sheet's people come from what the screen is showing. So if you're viewing the sheet as of a past date, its lines reflect that date, while the other sheets' lines always show their current figures. The request doesn't say which it should be, and the tests don't check it.

No stored data changes or audit records were needed: the search only reads, and the test expects no audit lines for it.

probe.probe_text:
I made no changes. Sources: the Java under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, the React app under `src/main/frontend/features/`, and the endpoint pipelines in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/`. ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them **Important:** every figure on the screen is calculated **in the browser**, mostly in `features/rates/rates.ts`. The server separately recalculates the same figures in Java (`Claim`, `LateCharge`, `Rounding`, `DatedSettings`, `RollupService`, `TakeStatement`, `PeriodCloser`). It uses those for settling, statements, period closes and the audit lines. ### Claim figures (per `claim-row`) | testid | Shows | Rule | |---|---|---| | `claim-status` | `ClaimStatus` | `DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED`. A clerk's settle above the clerk limit becomes `PENDING`, which a steward approves (`SETTLED`) or rejects (back to `OPEN`). `VOID` is final. `DELETED` applies to drafts only. | | `claim-number` | `number` | Given on **open** by `ClaimNumbers.next`: `FY-n`, counted across the sheet's whole tree, within the fiscal year the claim's **due-by** falls in (`fiscalStartMonth`). Once `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, numbers run per period instead: `-n`, or `X-n` outside any period. Numbers are never reused. A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned or transferred claim gets a new one. | | `claim-due-by` | `dueBy` | `NewDueBy`: the *terms*-th business day after the claim date, skipping weekends and holidays. Terms come from the person's own terms, else the grade's (`terms-`), else the sheet's (default 14), each as in force on the claim date. Fixed at creation. A re-date keeps it, an edit keeps it, and a split gets a fresh one. **But** adding a holiday re-fixes it (`RefixDueBys`) for every claim that isn't SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday. | | `claim-due` | `claimDue` / `Claim.due` | If settled, the frozen `due`. Otherwise `max(floorOn(date), figure + lateCharge)`. **figure** is the statement-bound `statedDue` when `bound()` (stated and not PENDING), else `amount × rate / 100`. The rate is `Rate.inForce` for the person's `gradeOn(date)` on the claim date, falling back to the parent sheet's rates; with no rate the figure is `n/a`. A correction gets no floor and no late charge. | | (rounding) | `Rounding.modeFor` / `roundingFor` | HALF_UP if the claim date is before `policyDate`, otherwise HALF_EVEN. A blank policy date means the **sheet's today**. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. | | (late charge) | `LateCharge.on` / `lateCharge` | Compounding. For each full 30 days past `dueBy + grace-`, it adds `latePctOn(boundary)` × (figure + earlier charges). A boundary at 0.00 adds nothing. Never charged on corrections or deferred claims. Never bound by a statement. | | `claim-overdue` | `overdue` | OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy + grace` is before today. | | `claim-deferred`, `-until` | `deferred(today)` | OPEN and today < `deferredUntil`. A deferred claim counts in no total, is never overdue, can't be settled or split, and isn't bound by a statement. | | `claim-stated` | `stated` | Set by the person's last statement. | | `claim-period` | `periodOf(dueBy)` | The period containing the claim's **due-by**, not its date. | | `claim-late-entry` | `lateEntry` | The claim was added while its due-by period was soft-closed. | | `claim-proofs`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-batch`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-log-line` | as stored | The log records status, user, today and the due at that moment (`LogClaimStatus`). | ### Person figures (per `person-row`) - **Which claims count** (`counts` / `Person.counts`): SETTLED always counts. OPEN or PENDING counts unless it is deferred, or a hold covers the claim date and no statement binds it (`heldOn`/`liveHolds`). Reaching the retirement date acts like a hold covering every date. DRAFT, VOID and DELETED never count. - `person-claimed`: the sum of the **amounts** of counting claims, leaving out corrections. - `person-due-total` (`personDue`): the sum of `claimDue` over counting claims, capped at the `cap` in force on today. It is `n/a` when the grade in force today has no rate today **and** no counting claim has any figure. - `person-excess`: how far the sum is above the cap (0.00 if not above, or if n/a). - `person-overdue-count` / `-total`: counting claims that are overdue, and their dues (late charges included). Not capped. - `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`personSplit`): counting dues split into SETTLED versus OPEN/PENDING. Not capped. - `person-aged-0-30|31-60|61`: dues of counting OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by days from the claim date to today. - `person-active`: has a counting OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to today. - `person-period-

-due-total` (`personPeriodDue`): claims whose **due-by** is in the period and that count by their status at the period's end (`statusAt`). Closed or soft-closed periods show the frozen `personTotals` (0.00 for anyone added since). - `person-backing`: for each patron, their SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days at the frozen `due`, × share / 100, summed, then rounded half-even. - `person-cut-total`: the sum of the person's pool cuts (`PoolResponse.cuts`). A pool pays out only when its shares total exactly 100.00 and there is a pot. Each cut is pot × share / (sum of shares that get a cut), rounded half-even. Retired or held members get 0.00, and the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut. Members whose dates exclude today are left out. - `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`, `person-grade` (`gradeOn(today)`), `person-terms`, `person-retired(-from)`, `person-hold-line`, `person-clashing`, `person-origin`: as stored. ### Sheet totals - `rollup-claimed-total`: everyone's claimed, summed. - `rollup-due-total` and `rollup-overdue-total` (`trimmedTotal`): people's figures summed, skipping n/a, and **dropping the single highest and lowest** when there are three or more. `header-due-total` and `header-overdue-total` use the same rule. - `rollup-overdue-count`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-cut-total`, `month--due-total`, `tag--due-total`: plain sums, not trimmed and not capped. A tag total counts a claim that has the tag itself or whose person has it. - `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`: the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user. - `consolidated-*`: this sheet plus all descendant sheets, each sheet's own trimmed totals added up. - `summary-grade--count|due-total|active`: retired people excluded. `summary-period-

-due-total|change`: change compared with the previous period by start date. `summary-status--count`, `summary-void--count`, `header-people-count` (includes retired people). - `rate-preview-count|diff`: how many OPEN/PENDING claims would change due under a candidate rate, and the total change. - `plan-generated-count`, `plan-next-dates`, `pool-total-share`, `pool-balanced`, `pool-cut`, `period-due-total` (frozen `closedTotal` once closed). ### Who may do what - **Viewer**: no changes at all (`CheckNotViewer` runs first in every write pipeline). **Archived sheet**: no changes (`CheckNotArchived`). - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions`): open, settle, void and close default to clerk + steward. Reassign and reopen default to steward. Split needs the "open" permission. - **Steward only, fixed in code**: approve and reject (reject needs a reason), re-settle, voiding a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of the last SETTLED log date), re-date, cancelling a statement, transfer, merge. A `Delegation` in force on today makes a user act as a steward. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim can't settle or approve it, and neither can its last editor (`editedBy`). - **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerkLimitOn` makes it PENDING instead. - **Proof threshold** (the grade's own, else the sheet's): with 0 proofs, settle and approve are refused. This is checked before the clerk limit. - **Note threshold**: opening a claim with an empty note is refused when its due is above the threshold. - **Period cap**: opening is refused once the person already has `cap` OPEN/PENDING claims due in that period. - **Void reasons**: when the sheet has a list, a void must pick one of them. - **Restore**: a deleted claim can only be restored on the same "today" it was deleted. **Remind**: once per today, OPEN/PENDING only. **Edit**: DRAFT only, and not while another user's editor lock is on it. **Lines**: a claim with lines takes its amount from them. ### What a date decides - **Claim date** decides: grade, rate, floor, terms, grace, proof and note thresholds, rounding mode, hold coverage, the retirement refusal, the month bucket, the age, the active window and the backing window. - **Due-by** decides: the period, the number sequence, overdue status and late-charge boundaries, closed-period refusals, late entry and the period cap. - **Today** decides: the n/a test, the cap, deferral, overdue status, late charge, whether retirement has been reached, delegations, and auto-close. Changing today also writes SNAPSHOT lines, records the sheet day, unlocks all editors and auto-closes any period whose to-date plus `graceDays` is before the new today. - **Entry date**: when set, a claim left blank takes it instead of today. - Dated settings (`DatedSettings`): the value in force is the one with the latest from-date on or before the date. Defaults are floor 1.00, late percent 0.00 and terms 14. ### Statements, holds, retirement, closed periods, imports - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds each counting claim to its *figure*, meaning the rate only, without floor or late charge. It unbinds the rest and records `statedTotal`, which is capped and includes floor and late charge. "As of" a date replays the sheet as it stood that day. A split or reassign drops a claim's binding. Cancelling unbinds all claims and goes back to the previous statement's total. - **Hold**: removes covered OPEN/PENDING, unbound claims from every live total and gives the person 0.00 pool cuts. It blocks no actions. - **Retirement**: claims dated after the retirement date are refused (add, reassign to the person, re-date, paste, plans). A past retirement refuses dates strictly inside it. Retired people can't be transferred or merged. - **Closed period** (by due-by): every change to its claims is refused, and so is adding a claim whose due-by would fall in it. Its totals are frozen. **Soft-close** freezes the totals but still allows changes; new claims are flagged as late entries. **Reopen** makes the totals live again. - **Imports and bulk adds**: - People import: a line matching an existing name or alias updates that person (grade recorded from today; terms and contact only if given). Otherwise it adds a person. - Rate import: replaces any rate with the same grade and from-date. - Paste: adds DRAFT claims; no corrections; a trailing ` #ref` becomes the reference. - Quick add: creates a new person at grade A if the name is unknown. - Plans: add DRAFTs up to the earlier of the plan's end and today; a refused date is skipped and retried next time. Imports, paste and quick add are all-or-nothing. - **Audit**: ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines (`RollupLines`) follow most changes. ALERT is written when a person's due-total crosses `alertThreshold`. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. Each piece is well commented, but the logic is scattered and duplicated: - **Two copies of the due math.** The same rules exist in Java and TypeScript. Totals are built separately in about 4 server places and about 15 React components. - **Rules are split up.** Business checks live in roughly 100 single-method step classes, and which checks apply to an action is only visible in the YAML pipelines. - **Comments disagree with the code.** I found at least five cases: - Docs say due-by never changes after creation, but adding a holiday re-fixes it. - Docs say "sheet-wide numbers 1, 2…", but numbers are now `FY-n`. - `PeriodCloser` and `ClaimLateEntry` say "dated in" a period, but the code uses due-by. - A settled claim voided after its period ended is dropped from the period total in Java (`Period.counts`) but still counted on screen (`countsInPeriod`). - "Cap" means two different things: a person's due-total cap and a period's open-claim cap. "Grace" also has two meanings: per-grade grace days for overdue, and sheet `graceDays` for auto-closing periods. A new developer would need to read both stacks side by side to trust any figure.
